summary: Frequent 429 Too Many Requests after launch; customer unsure about rate limits + retry behavior
related_confluence_pages: Known issues: 429 throttling and quota misconfiguration
Escalation Playbook v2: Severity matrix and triage criteria
description:
## Customer report
Customer launched a new feature and is seeing frequent HTTP 429 responses from Redwood API. They are unsure what limits apply (org vs project vs key), and whether they should retry 429s vs treat as hard-fail.

## Impact
- End-user requests intermittently fail during traffic bursts.
- Customer reports 10–25% of requests returning 429 during peak periods.
- No evidence of 5xx; customer perceives service as unstable.

## Environment
- Deployment: Hosted API (self-serve)
- Region: us-west
- Models: rw-chat-1 (chat completions), rw-embed-1 (embeddings)
- Client: Python + server-side concurrency (async workers)

## What the customer is seeing
Example error (from customer):
- HTTP status: 429
- Body: {"error": {"type": "rate_limit", "message": "Too many requests"}}
- They are currently retrying immediately (no backoff) up to 3 times.

## Initial triage checklist
- Confirm whether 429 is quota exhaustion vs burst rate limit.
- Confirm customer is using multiple API keys / multiple processes.
- Request request-ids for sampling and verify on gateway logs.
- Validate whether retries are amplifying the load (thundering herd).

## Requested from customer
- 5–10 request_ids from 429 responses (with timestamps)
- Peak QPS and typical request pattern (chat vs embeddings)
- Current timeout + retry configuration

## Support notes (internal)
This appears consistent with self-serve project limits being exceeded post-launch + overly aggressive retry behavior. Not an incident unless we observe elevated 429 rates platform-wide or incorrect enforcement.

Next actions:
1) Check org/project quota + burst settings in Console.
2) Provide standard retry/backoff guidance and token-bucket explanation.
3) Offer options: request limit increase, smoothing concurrency, or Dedicated if sustained throughput is required.
comments: 2026-02-11 18:22Z — Priya Shah (Support) — Acknowledged ticket. Asked customer for request_ids from 429 responses, timestamps, and peak concurrency/QPS. Also asked whether they are batching or sending one request per end-user event.

2026-02-11 19:03Z — Customer — Provided 8 request_ids (redacted here) spanning 18:40–18:55Z. Peak traffic: ~120 req/min chat, ~300 req/min embeddings. They have 12 gunicorn workers and an async queue; retries are immediate with no jitter. They assumed 429 indicates transient failure and should be retried instantly.

2026-02-11 19:28Z — Owen Phillips (Support Eng) — Reviewed request_ids in gateway logs (us-west). 429s are rate_limit type, not auth failures. Pattern shows short bursts exceeding project-level request rate + token rate. Retried requests are landing within the same 1s window, multiplying the burst. No abnormal 5xx/latency observed in region. This is expected enforcement, not a platform incident.

2026-02-11 19:41Z — Owen Phillips (Support Eng) — Checked Console limits: customer is on default self-serve project caps. Their new traffic profile exceeds burst capacity during minute-level peaks. Proposed mitigations: (a) exponential backoff with jitter on 429, (b) cap in-flight requests per worker, (c) optionally enable client-side queueing to smooth bursts, (d) request quota increase if usage is legitimate and sustained.

2026-02-11 20:02Z — Priya Shah (Support) — Sent customer guidance: 429 means you have exceeded an enforced rate limit/quota; safe to retry with backoff+jitter and honoring Retry-After header if present. Recommended starting with base delay 250–500ms, exponential backoff (2x) up to ~10–15s, max retry attempts 5, and adding random jitter. Also advised not to retry streaming requests mid-stream; instead, re-issue a new request after backoff.

2026-02-12 09:10Z — Customer — Implemented backoff + jitter and reduced concurrency per worker. 429 rate dropped significantly; still seeing occasional spikes during campaign email sends. Asked if limits can be increased and where to view them clearly.

2026-02-12 10:05Z — Owen Phillips (Support Eng) — Walked customer through where limits appear in Console (org vs project). Confirmed they can request a higher self-serve quota; created internal note to ensure consistent field naming in Support template (ties to INT-1337). Provided additional guidance: if they have predictable daily peaks, they can implement a token bucket locally to smooth bursts and avoid retries storming the gateway.

2026-02-12 10:32Z — Priya Shah (Support) — Updated customer with next steps: we can submit a quota increase request after confirming sustained usage and expected peak traffic. In the meantime, recommended keeping retry policy and setting a hard cap on concurrent requests per API key. Shared KB draft link for 429 troubleshooting (to be published) and confirmed this is not a service outage.
2026-02-12 17:20Z — Customer — Confirmed 429s are now rare and handled gracefully. Requested quota increase review for next week; ok to close current ticket.

2026-02-12 17:34Z — Priya Shah (Support) — Resolved. Summary: 429s were expected rate-limit enforcement under bursty traffic; immediate retries amplified the issue. Mitigation validated: exponential backoff + jitter + reduced concurrency. Follow-up: quota increase request handled separately if needed; referencing upcoming SDK/doc improvements.
resolution: Validated 429s were due to self-serve project rate limits being exceeded during launch traffic bursts. Customer changed retry strategy from immediate retry to exponential backoff with jitter (and reduced in-flight concurrency), which reduced 429 impact to rare/handled events. Provided Console guidance on viewing limits and offered quota increase path if sustained throughput requires it. No platform incident.
internal_follow_ups: Ensure Support ticket template captures: peak QPS/concurrency, retry policy, and whether customer honors Retry-After (INT-1337 reference).
Track SDK default retry/backoff guidance improvements (redwood-sdk-python#519).
Add/refresh KB entry for 429 troubleshooting and quota/rate-limit explanation (Known issues: 429 throttling and quota misconfiguration).
